title: GreenGateway Connection Write Model
description: Version 0.1 write model for a logical upstream Connection. It contains opaque secret references only and never resolved secret material.

additional_headers.description: Secret-backed headers injected alongside the primary credential, in this order, on every credentialed lane (tools, proxy, MCP, discovery, test). Each header name must be a non-reserved HTTP header name (never Authorization), must not name the primary credential's header, and must be unique within the list; names are normalized to lowercase. Adding, removing, or changing an entry is a secrets write.

caller_assertion.description: Attests the calling principal to the upstream on every manual HTTP, managed OpenAPI and managed MCP tool call, every request a composite tool sends and every proxied request made through this Connection, alongside the primary credential rather than instead of it: the credential says which system is calling, the assertion says on whose behalf, so an upstream the operator controls can apply its own per-user checks. Per request the gateway signs one short-lived JWT naming the validated principal (sub is the identity provider's issuer, '#', and its subject; jti is the gateway request ID, with '.' and a sequence number for each request of a managed MCP tool call's session and each leaf request of a composite tool) and writes it, as the last header, in header_name; with bind_request it also binds the method, the request target and the SHA-256 of the exact body sent. A call with no principal to name, a service token included, is refused with caller_assertion_no_principal before any network or secret I/O. The endpoint must use https. Lanes with no caller to attest (discovery, enum and label sources, stored tests) are refused with caller_assertion_not_enforced, as is every lane but manual tools and stored tests, which run as the principal who asks for them, on a delegated_issuer_token Connection and every lane for a stored block only an earlier release accepted. Saving an enabled Connection resolves its signing key and every published key, from whichever secret source holds it, and loads each for its algorithm; a key that cannot be used refuses the save, and every call reads and loads the signing key again. The public halves of every enabled Connection's keys are served at /.well-known/caller-assertion-jwks.json, which the upstream verifies against. A stored Connection whose keys can no longer be used is left out of that set, with a diagnostic, rather than stopping the gateway, and its calls are refused with caller_assertion_key_not_published until its keys load again. Omit the block to send only the credential.

signing_key_id.description: Secret alias holding the private key as exactly one PKCS#8 PEM block (BEGIN PRIVATE KEY): a P-256 key for es256, an RSA key of at least 2048 bits for rs256. Resolved with the assertion_signing_key purpose, so it comes from an operator alias or an external secret provider, never the encrypted local store; a key of the other algorithm is refused as algorithm_mismatch.

kid.description: JOSE kid, published in the gateway's JWKS so an upstream can select the right key and keys can rotate without a flag day. Name one key only: never put new key material behind a kid that is already published.

algorithm.description: Signature algorithm. Both are offered because verifier libraries and platform documentation differ on which is convenient.

token_type.description: JOSE typ. Naming the intended use stops a token minted for one upstream being replayed at another that trusts the same keys.

header_name.description: Header carrying the assertion. Must be a non-reserved HTTP header name and must differ, case-insensitively, from the header the primary credential uses and from every additional header name; normalized to lowercase.

lifetime_seconds.description: An assertion is a bearer credential for as long as it is valid, so this is a replay window rather than a convenience setting.

claims.description: Principal fields to attest beyond sub, which is always present. A closed set rather than free-form templating, so a configuration mistake cannot attest something a caller supplied.

bind_request.description: Include the method, path and a SHA-256 of the body actually sent, so an assertion cannot be lifted onto different arguments. The digest covers the transmitted bytes, not a canonical form, so an upstream verifies it with its standard library.

bind_approval.description: Reserved: would require, and include, the approval that authorised a mutation. No approval subsystem exists yet, so only false is accepted.

published_keys.description: Keys published in the JWKS beside the signing key that never sign: the next key, published before the switch so every verifier already holds it, and the previous one, kept until every assertion it signed has expired. Each kid and each alias may appear once across the signing key and this list.

signing_key_id.description: Secret alias holding the private key, in the same form as the signing key. The gateway derives and publishes its public half; nothing is ever signed with it while it is listed here.

stable_id.description: Opaque URL-safe identifier. Environment names, filesystem paths, and provider locators are not accepted by the admin connection model.

oneOf.description: The calling user's own upstream token, obtained per caller from a trusted issuer by OAuth 2.0 token exchange (RFC 8693) and injected as Authorization: Bearer, instead of one service credential shared by every caller. On a cache miss the gateway POSTs grant_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange to token_exchange_url, authenticated with client_secret_basic, with requested_token_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token and, as the subject token (subject_token_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt), a JWT signed with this Connection's caller_assertion key naming the validated caller exactly as a caller assertion does, which the issuer verifies against /.well-known/caller-assertion-jwks.json. The caller's own inbound bearer token is never forwarded. The issued token is cached per caller until shortly before its expires_in, for at most 900 seconds. A call with no principal, a service token included, is refused with delegated_token_no_principal; an issuer refusal with delegated_token_denied; any other exchange failure with delegated_token_exchange_failed. Requires kind http_api and a caller_assertion block without bind_request; the assertion is sent to the issuer only, never upstream. Only manual HTTP tool calls are served, and stored Connection tests, which exchange the testing principal's own token inline and cache nothing.

token_exchange_url.description: The issuer's RFC 8693 endpoint. HTTPS only, without userinfo, query or fragment, and checked against the egress allowlist on every exchange before any secret is read.

client_secret_id.description: Secret alias of the client secret the gateway authenticates to the issuer with, resolved with the token_exchange_client_secret purpose, so it comes from an operator alias or an external secret provider, never the encrypted local store. No other field of any Connection may bind the same alias. Required once the Connection is enabled.

requested_scopes.description: Sent as the space-separated scope parameter. Prefer read-only scopes: the issuer hands out exactly what is asked for.

audience.description: RFC 8693 audience: the logical name of the upstream the token is for.

resource.description: RFC 8693 resource: the URI of the upstream the token is for.

revocation_url.description: The issuer's OAuth 2.0 token revocation endpoint (RFC 7009). HTTPS only, without userinfo, query or fragment, and checked against the egress allowlist before the client secret is read. When set, a token purged from the cache, because an operator purged its principal or a validator refused one of the principal's credentials as revoked, is also revoked here once, best effort, with the same client credentials. Absent, a purged token is only dropped and stays valid at the issuer until it expires.

subject_token_source.description: What names the caller to the issuer. caller_assertion, the only value, is a JWT the gateway signs with this Connection's caller_assertion key.

oneOf.description: The calling user's own Google Workspace token, obtained per caller by domain-wide delegation and injected as Authorization: Bearer, instead of one service credential shared by every caller. On a cache miss the gateway builds a JWT claim set (iss the service account, sub the caller's email, scope the space-separated scopes, aud https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, iat, and exp 300 seconds later), has Google sign it as the service account through the IAM Credentials signJwt method, authenticated as the federated identity of workload_identity_profile, so no service-account key is held by the gateway, checks the signed claims are exactly those sent, and exchanges it at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token with grant_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer. Both endpoints are fixed and must be egress-allowlisted; each is checked before the federated identity is read. The token is cached per caller until shortly before Google's expires_in and for at most 900 seconds, and every mint is audited as connection.google_delegation_token with the caller as actor and no token material. Requires kind http_api and no caller_assertion. Only manual HTTP tool calls, and a stored Connection test run as the principal who asks for it with a token minted for that request alone, are served; every other lane is refused with authentication_not_supported. A call with no principal, a service token included, is refused with delegated_token_no_principal; a caller attested by an issuer outside subject_issuers with google_delegation_issuer_not_trusted; one without an email with google_delegation_no_email; all before any request. A delegated service account can act as every user of the domain for its scopes: use a dedicated account and read-only scopes.

service_account_email.description: The delegated service account, a dedicated name@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com account a Workspace super-admin authorised for scopes. The federated identity must hold roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on it.

workload_identity_profile.description: The id of a CONNECTION_GCP_PROVIDER profile: the workload identity that signs as the service account. A reference to trusted startup configuration, never a token file, audience or key. Saving an enabled Connection requires the profile to be configured.

scopes.description: Sent as the space-separated scope claim, sorted. Must be within what the Workspace administrator authorised for the service account; prefer read-only scopes.

subject_claim.description: Which attested claim becomes sub. email, the only value, is the validated principal's email.

subject_issuers.description: The identity providers trusted to name Workspace users by email, compared with the principal's canonical issuer (a trailing slash is ignored). Any configured provider can put any address in its tokens, so list only the one authoritative for the domain.

secret_id.description: Opaque ID of a header_api_key secret. Required once the Connection is enabled; a disabled draft may omit it.

method.description: New writes allow only GET or HEAD. Previously persisted v0 OPTIONS profiles remain readable for upgrade compatibility, but are not accepted by this write schema or executed by the Connection test endpoint.
